headline: KINROSS BEATS EPS BUT LOWERS 2026-27 PRODUCTION OUTLOOK — AISC Surges 20% to $1,947/oz; Revenue Misses at $1.77B Despite $4,249 Average Gold Price
snippet: Kinross Gold Q3 2026: adjusted EPS of $0.50 beat the FactSet/Zacks consensus of $0.46-0.47, but revenue fell 2% to $1.77 billion — missing estimates — and production dropped to 424,693 gold-equivalent ounces from 503,862 a year earlier. The bigger news is a formal reduction in both 2026 and 2027 gold production guidance, a notable cut at a moment when gold near $4,000 should be generating peak profits; all-in sustaining costs surged 20% to $1,947/oz despite the $4,249 average realized price.

headline: TECK TOPS Q3 ESTIMATES ON COPPER STRENGTH — Beat Arrives Before Highland Valley Strike Hit the Books; Q4 Guidance Now at Risk With 1,200 Workers Still Idled
snippet: Teck Resources beat analyst earnings estimates in Q3 2026 on stronger copper performance, releasing results before market open today. The quarter ended September 30 — meaning the Highland Valley Copper strike (commenced October 24) had zero impact on Q3 numbers. Investors are now focused on Q4 guidance, where the ongoing work stoppage at Canada's largest open-pit copper mine creates material production uncertainty for the final quarter of 2026.

headline: FED HOLDS RATES WITH TWO HAWKISH DISSENTS — Gold Closes Flat at $4,057 After Initial 2% Spike; Silver Slides 1%, G/S Ratio Stretches to 75
snippet: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at its October 28 meeting, but two policymakers voted for an immediate hike — a more hawkish signal than markets expected. Gold spiked 2% intraday on the hold before handing back most gains to close nearly flat at $4,056.80, while silver fell over 1% to around $53.72. The gold-to-silver ratio pushed to approximately 75, up from roughly 60 at the start of 2026, as silver continues to underperform the metal it should be tracking higher.

headline: TREY REIK'S GOLD CALL VINDICATED BY FED HOLD — '$4,000 Is Not Speculative'; De-Dollarization Thesis Intact 26% Below January Record
snippet: Analyst Trey Reik, who predicted in January 2026 that gold would break $4,000 driven by structural de-dollarization and central bank accumulation, gets his thesis revisited following the Fed's October 28 hold. The piece argues that gold sustaining the $4,000 level through a hawkish central bank cycle validates the structural bull case — even as the metal sits roughly 26% below its January record near $5,400/oz and miner equities have underperformed the metal sharply.

headline: NEWCORE GOLD DRILLS 37m AT 2.16 g/t AU IN GHANA — High-Grade 9m Core at 5.10 g/t Confirms Depth Continuity at Enchi; More Assays Pending (TSXV:NCAU)
snippet: Newcore Gold (TSXV:NCAU) reported hole NBDD093 returning 2.16 g/t gold over 37.0 metres from 205 metres depth at its Enchi Gold Project in Ghana, with a high-grade 5.10 g/t core over 9.0 metres. The result extends depth continuity at the multi-million-ounce Enchi deposit in a jurisdiction with established gold mining infrastructure; additional assays from the ongoing drill program are pending.

headline: FIRST QUANTUM Q3 COPPER CLIMBS 8% TO 108,959 TONNES — Sequential Recovery Continues as Zambian Operations Improve; Full-Year Outlook Under Review
snippet: First Quantum Minerals reported Q3 2026 copper production of 108,959 tonnes, up 8% from 100,487 tonnes in Q2, as its African operations continued a recovery path. The sequential improvement signals ongoing stabilization after a challenging stretch; the full-year production outlook update will be closely watched given the company's significant exposure to copper prices near $6.63/lb.

headline: NORTHERN STAR'S NEW CEO SIGNALS OPENNESS TO IMPROVED GOLD FIELDS BID — A$38.7B Offer Rejected as Undervalued; Gold Fields Eyes Higher Cash Component After Australian Roadshow
snippet: Northern Star Resources' new CEO Suresh Vadnagra, who took the helm October 5, signalled the board would engage with Gold Fields if it improves its A$38.7 billion (~$27 billion) takeover proposal — the unsolicited approach was initially rejected as 'highly opportunistic' and undervalued. Gold Fields is conducting an Australian investor roadshow in late October to gauge support for an improved bid; analysts note Australian major takeovers typically require a 30%+ premium to close, while the implied value of Gold Fields' current offer has slipped to roughly 14% premium as its own share price declined.

headline: GOLD MINERS' RSI FALLS TO 28-33 — Wheaton Precious at 37% Discount to Analyst Target; Newmont, Kinross Screen Oversold Heading Into Earnings Season
snippet: A new Investing.com analysis finds major gold miners trading at RSI readings of 28-33 — extreme oversold territory — with Wheaton Precious Metals at $125.92 against an analyst consensus target of $173.17 (37% implied upside), and Newmont and Kinross also at deeply discounted multiples of 11.5x and 9.1x forward earnings. The piece cautions that oversold readings don't guarantee a reversal and cites analysis warning miners could fall a further 20-30% before a durable capitulation low forms.

headline: EMPEROR METALS EXTENDS DUQUESNE WEST WITH 26.3m AT 1.0 g/t — 15 More Holes Awaiting Assay at Quebec Gold Project; Step-Outs Strengthen Open-Pit Case (TSXV:EPML)
snippet: Emperor Metals (TSXV:EPML) released additional assays from seven Duquesne West holes in Quebec, with results including 26.3 metres at 1.0 g/t gold. Assays remain pending for 15 more holes from the ongoing program; step-out drilling has been progressively expanding the mineralized footprint at this near-surface gold project that the company is positioning for open-pit development.

headline: GLOBAL ENERGY METALS MAPS MULTIPLE URANIUM TARGETS AT TERRA NORTH — Early-Stage Anomalies in Saskatchewan's Uranium District; Royalty Covers 594 km² of Ground
snippet: Global Energy Metals identified multiple uranium exploration targets at its Terra North project in Saskatchewan, adding early-stage upside to a critical minerals portfolio that also includes a royalty over approximately 594 square kilometres of uranium-prospective ground in Canada's premier uranium district. The targets are anomalies requiring follow-up investigation to establish drill priority — and arrive at a time when the uranium long-term contract price has climbed to a record US$96 per pound in Q3 2026.
